summary: Explicit local/global accommodation and proxy-policy comparisons: different truth/accessibility predictions, world-preserving versus assignment-preserving permissions, and complete allowed/blocked runs.
implementation_scope: Policy comparison step 2 for named repair requests and supported modal/proxy programs; no policy selected as the source's default or a complete theory of appropriateness.

sources.citation: Heim, I. (1982). The Semantics of Definite and Indefinite Noun Phrases. Consulted Schoubye–Glick 2011 retypesetting, pp.244–246 and 247–252.
sources.available: Relevant primary-source passages read; independent semantic review pending.

definitions_mapped.source: pp.245–246 options (a)/(b), applied to fresh descriptive accommodation under negation.
Added explicit selector and certificates for an identified fresh repair request; not a general accommodation search algorithm.
Added comparison bounds and permission-order infrastructure, not source appropriateness rules.
Alternative restrictions motivated by pp.250–252; distinguish preserved world content from literal satisfaction-set preservation. Neither declared to be the complete source policy.
New fixed-input diagnostics and instantiations of the source's king/factivity discussions. Keep-all attention is held fixed as an instrumentation fixture.

evidence: General source formulas and named conditional policy comparisons are proved; see campaigns/heim_1982_policy_results.md.
simplifications: The examples use a fixed keep-all attention fixture and named descriptions; finite countermodels do not restrict the general theorems.
omissions: No empirical preference ranking or complete appropriateness/recency/bridge-selection theory.
No proof that these alternatives exhaust every reasonable completion of Heim.
additions: Explicit alternative policy definitions, inclusion/strictness proofs and complete-run diagnostics.

determination_rationale: Different completions have demonstrably different predictions. This identifies additional commitments, not which completion is correct or whether whole-source restructuring is necessary.

artifact_classes.description: Policy selectors and run-comparison infrastructure; no substrate obstruction or necessity-of-restructuring inferred.

notes: Prior research preserved. New theory commitments are explicitly labeled and none adopted. Counts include helpers and diagnostics; probe flags retained. See policy results and manifest.
